claims_supported: Mixed Armistice Commission majority found a major, unprovoked and premeditated Israeli regular-army attack on Jordanian territory near Husan on 25–26 September; records 12 National Guards killed near Husan, two civilians wounded, attack at Wadi Fukin and school demolition, plus additional losses at Sharafa police post and Khader village
limitations: Israeli delegation absent and opposed the Commission's characterization; different areas and military/civilian casualty categories must remain distinct. Armistice decision is not a criminal verdict.

title: Letter from Jordan concerning Israeli attacks on villages, 25–26 September and 10–11 October 1956 (S/3678)
author_or_issuing_body: Jordanian representative to the UN Security Council
source_type: contemporaneous state complaint to the Security Council
claims_supported: Jordan's report says 25 Jordanians were killed and six wounded in the Husan-area attack, including a 70-year-old civilian and 12-year-old girl killed and a seven-year-old girl wounded; records the October Qalqiliya attack complaint
limitations: Party submission; its aggregate 25 dead differs from the later disaggregated MAC findings for Husan, Wadi Fukin, Sharafa and Khader; not all casualties were civilians.

title: UNTSO report on Qalqiliya attack of 10–11 October 1956 (S/3685)
author_or_issuing_body: United Nations Truce Supervision Organization; Chief of Staff
claims_supported: UN observers documented Israeli forces attacking the Qalqiliya police post, shelling the town, demolishing the police post and water pumping house, damaging homes and school, and reported 48 Jordanian dead (43 military/guards/police, 3 civilians, 2 unidentified); Israel reported 18 force members dead
limitations: Commission meeting was not completed and Israeli delegation was absent. The 48 is not a civilian toll. UN observers reported one child and one woman killed in the town; casualty categories in narrative/overall count require care.

title: Israelis destroy Jordanian stronghold in seven-hour battle
claims_supported: Reports Israeli raid on Qalqiliya police stronghold, Jordanian casualty claim and UN observers' later count of 48 Jordanian bodies
limitations: Early report includes a Jordanian complaint and preliminary numbers; consult UNTSO report for final observed military/civilian categories.

title: Middle East debate
author_or_issuing_body: United Kingdom House of Commons / Hansard
claims_supported: UK Foreign Secretary cited approximately 39 deaths in the Husan raid and 48 in the Qalqiliya raid
limitations: Parliamentary summary gives a Husan estimate differing from the UN Jordan complaint and MAC disaggregated report; preserve as a separate report, not an additional count.

title: The 1956–57 Occupation of the Gaza Strip: Israeli Proposals to Resettle the Palestinian Refugees
author_or_issuing_body: Nur Masalha / British Journal of Middle Eastern Studies
claims_supported: Examines Israeli proposals during the 1956–57 occupation for resettlement of Gaza refugees outside the Strip; relevant to expansionist/territorial policy and forced-transfer concerns
limitations: Documents proposals and planning, not proof that the proposed transfers were executed in 1956; attribute plans to the author and distinguish them from actual displacement.

title: Report by Acting Chief of Staff of UNTSO concerning Government House neutral zone
author_or_issuing_body: United Nations Truce Supervision Organization; Colonel B.V. Leary
source_type: contemporaneous UN investigation and Security Council report
claims_supported: Israeli laborers staked out neutral-zone land from 21 July; cut roads and ploughed land for stated afforestation project; 50–60 olive trees uprooted; armed Israeli Border Police protected workers; Israel had progressively extended cultivation since 1949; zone appeared predominantly Arab-owned in UNCCP records but specific titles required research; UNTSO unable to authoritatively decide civilian land-use dispute; report also documents Jordanian military presence/traffic
limitations: Specific ownership of trees and parcels requires title search; Israel argued work was permissible civilian activity; Jordan alleged armed incursions; UNTSO recorded military infractions by both sides and recommended suspension pending negotiation; not a criminal finding

title: Message from Secretary of State Dulles to Prime Minister Ben Gurion
author_or_issuing_body: United States Department of State / Foreign Relations of the United States
claims_supported: U.S. Secretary of State said Israel continued tree planting despite U.S. requests for suspension; noted UNTSO recommended work stop pending peaceful resolution
limitations: Records U.S. position and summary of UNTSO recommendation; does not establish title or legal violation

title: Letter from Gaza
author_or_issuing_body: A. J. Liebling / The New Yorker
claims_supported: Reports Israeli forces occupied Gaza until March 1957 withdrawal; author says forces removed twenty-five families during withdrawal; gives UNRWA population stock of 219423 refugees in Gaza
limitations: Does not identify families destination voluntariness or legal basis; population stock is not new displacement flow

title: Security Council Resolution 127 on Government House zone
claims_supported: Says neither Israel nor Jordan had sovereignty over zone; directs UNTSO to regulate civilian use with regard to ownership and bars using other party nationals property absent agreement
limitations: 1958 follow-up not 1957 finding; does not determine criminal responsibility or specific parcel title

title: Palestinian Internally Displaced Persons inside Israel: Challenging the Solid Structures
source_type: Palestinian historical research article with endnotes citing earlier scholarship and Israeli archives
claims_supported: Endnote reports 1957 deportation of al-Syajj Arabs, citing Cohen (2001) and Wakim (2001); another endnote reports October 1958 confiscation of about 56 Tamra plots to resettle IDPs, citing Cohen and Israel State Archives Housing Ministry file 4410/61621
limitations: Secondary source; underlying studies/archive file not reviewed; gives neither al-Syajj deportee count nor Tamra affected-person count

title: Report on firing incident of 26 May 1958 on Mount Scopus (S/4030)
author_or_issuing_body: UNTSO Chief of Staff / United Nations Security Council
source_type: Contemporaneous UNTSO report based on observer accounts and party investigations
claims_supported: Reports disputed 26 May firing exchange; records Israeli and Jordanian accounts, observer findings, casualties and Issawiya-Israel police tensions; observers did not confirm firing from within Issawiya village
limitations: The initial firing attribution is unresolved; four Israelis were killed and two wounded in the exchange; do not present the report as a finding that Israel initiated it

title: Addendum to report on firing incident of 26 May 1958 on Mount Scopus (S/4030/Add.1)
author_or_issuing_body: UNTSO Chief of Staff / United Nations Security Council
source_type: Contemporaneous UNTSO addendum reporting observer follow-up
claims_supported: Reports that the only reasonable road available to Issawiya villagers was closed by Israeli authorities on 1 June; an UN observer directly saw Israeli police fire on villagers on 2 June, killing one man
limitations: The incident report does not identify the dead villager; preserve as a separate event from the unresolved 26 May exchange; not a criminal judgment

title: 100 Jordanians Seek to Enter Israel Territory on Mt. Scopus; One Wounded
source_type: Contemporary foreign news report relaying Israeli spokesman's account
claims_supported: Israeli spokesman told JTA police fired at a group approaching a roadblock on 3 June; one person was reported wounded; Israeli officials claimed the group was armed and Jordanian-led
limitations: Official claims and injury are not independently verified by the dispatch; the 3 June event is separate from the UN-observed 2 June killing
